title: National Landslide Preparedness Act
official_summary:
National Landslide Preparedness Act

This bill directs the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS) to establish a National Landslide Hazards Reduction Program to identify and understand landslide hazards and risks, reduce losses from landslides, protect communities at risk of landslide hazards, and help improve communication and emergency preparedness.

The USGS shall, among other things

  • develop and publish a national strategy for landslide hazards, risk reduction, and response in the United States (including territories);
  • develop and maintain a publicly accessible national landslide hazard and risk inventory database;
  • expand the early warning system for debris flow; and
  • establish emergency response procedures for the rapid deployment of federal scientists, equipment, and services to areas impacted by a significant landslide event.

The USGS may provide grants to research, map, assess, and collect data on landslide hazards.

The National Science Foundation may provide grants to eligible entities for landslide research.

The USGS (1) shall advance the identification, mapping, research, and monitoring of subsidence and groundwater resource accounting, particularly in areas affected by drought; (2) shall establish the 3D Elevation Program and the 3D Elevation Federal Interagency Coordinating Committee; and (3) may make grants and enter into cooperative agreements to facilitate the improvement of nationwide coverage of 3D elevation data.

summary.headline: This law directs the U.S. Geological Survey to run a national program on landslide hazards and to build related mapping, data, and emergency response tools.
summary.what_it_does: The law creates a National Landslide Hazards Reduction Program within the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS). The USGS must publish a national landslide strategy, maintain a public database of landslide hazards and risks, expand an early warning system for debris flows, and set up procedures to quickly send federal scientists and equipment to places hit by major landslides. The law also lets the USGS and the National Science Foundation give grants for landslide research and mapping, and it sets up work on land subsidence, groundwater tracking, and a 3D elevation data program.

who_it_affects.group: Communities in areas at risk of landslides
who_it_affects.how: They can use the public national hazard and risk database and early warning system that the USGS must build and expand.

who_it_affects.group: Residents of areas affected by drought or land subsidence
who_it_affects.how: The USGS must study and map subsidence and track groundwater resources in these areas.

who_it_affects.group: State, local, and territorial emergency managers
who_it_affects.how: They may receive federal scientists, equipment, and services after a significant landslide, under the new response procedures.
They may apply for USGS or National Science Foundation grants to study landslide hazards and collect data.
The USGS may fund nationwide 3D elevation data coverage through grants and cooperative agreements.
